name: Yellow Stem Borer (Scirpophaga incertulas)
symptoms: Dead hearts in vegetative stage, White ears in reproductive/flowering stage. Holes in stem with frass.
biological_cultural_control: Set up light traps (1/ha) and pheromone traps (5/ha) with Scirpolure. Conserve egg parasitoid Trichogramma japonicum (100,000/ha).
chemical_control: Apply Cartap hydrochloride 4G @ 25 kg/ha or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 150 ml/ha when pest reaches ETL (1 moth/m2 or 5% dead heart).

name: Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae)
symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical spots with grey/white center and brown-red margin on leaves; neck blast turns node black and panicle falls over.
biological_cultural_control: Avoid excessive nitrogen application; split N in 3-4 doses. Treat seed with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg seed. Burn infected stubbles.
chemical_control: Foliar spray of Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L or Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1 ml/L at initial symptom appearance.

name: Wheat Rust (Yellow/Stripe Rust - Puccinia striiformis)
symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules arranged in linear stripes/rows on leaf blades, leaf sheaths, and glumes. Dust-like spores rub off on fingers.
biological_cultural_control: Plant resistant cultivars (e.g., DBW-187, DBW-303, HD-3226). Avoid early sowing in sub-montane belts. Crop rotation.
chemical_control: Foliar spray with Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 1 ml/L of water or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1 ml/L as soon as stripes appear.

name: Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
symptoms: Concentric ring spots ('target board' appearance) on older lower leaves. Leaves yellow and drop. Dark sunken stem lesions.
biological_cultural_control: Mulching to prevent soil splash; remove and destroy lower infected leaves; 3-year non-solanaceous crop rotation; drip irrigation instead of sprinkler.
chemical_control: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 ml/L at 10-14 day intervals.

name: Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV)
symptoms: Upward curling, puckering, crinkling, thickening and severe reduction of leaf size. Stunted plant growth, bushy appearance, failed fruit set.
biological_cultural_control: Grow nursery under 40-mesh insect-proof nylon nets. Install yellow sticky traps (15/ha) to trap whitefly vectors. Spray neem oil (5 ml/L).
chemical_control: Control whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci) using Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L.

name: Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda)
symptoms: Ragged shot holes and large irregular feeding scars on leaves, whorl damage filled with moist sawdust-like fecal matter.
biological_cultural_control: Deep summer ploughing; intercrop with cowpea/desmodium; release egg parasitoid Trichogramma pretiosum @ 50,000/acre; apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 2 g/L.
chemical_control: Whorl application of Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4 ml/L or Emamectin benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4 g/L during early larval instars.
source: ICAR-National Bureau of Agricultural Insect Resources

name: Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella)
symptoms: Rosetted flowers ('rosette flower effect'), premature dropping of squares/bolls, burrowing inside developing bolls damaging lint and seeds.
biological_cultural_control: Destroy cotton stalks after harvest; avoid ratoon cropping; install delta traps with Gossyplure pheromone (5/ha) to monitor ETL (8 moths/trap/night).
chemical_control: Spray Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 2.5 ml/L or Profenofos 50% EC @ 2 ml/L or Spinosad 45% SC @ 0.3 ml/L at peak flowering and boll formation.

name: Wilt Disease (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ciceris)
symptoms: Drooping of petioles and rachis, yellowing and drying of leaves starting from top to bottom. Vascular browning visible when stem is split vertically.
biological_cultural_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 5-10 g/kg seed. Adopt deep summer ploughing, crop rotation with non-hosts (sorghum, mustard).
chemical_control: Seed dressing with Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP @ 2 g/kg seed prior to sowing. Once symptoms appear in field, systemic fungicides have limited efficacy.
